```{r setup, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(collapse = TRUE, comment = "#>", eval = FALSE)
library(PGViS)
```

This covers stages 1–6: aligned reads to a BED of variants intersected with
regulatory regions and dbSNP. None of it runs in a vignette (it needs GATK, a
reference genome and a scheduler), so every chunk here is `eval = FALSE`.

## The shape of it

```{r stages, eval = TRUE}
pgvis_stages()[, c("stage", "description")]
```

Each stage is a shell template with no site-specific paths in it.
`pgvis_render_script()` prepends a generated variable block and, on SLURM, the
`#SBATCH` directives. You get a plain executable script — read it, edit it,
run it by hand if you prefer.

## Configuration

```{r config}
cfg <- pgvis_config(
  root            = "/scratch/me/lung_pgvis",
  reference_fasta = "/refs/hg38.fa",
  dbsnp_dir       = "/refs/dbsnp155/by_chr",
  regions   = list(acceptor = "/refs/acceptor_sorted.bed",
                   donor    = "/refs/donor_sorted.bed"),
  tfbs_dir  = "/refs/encode_tfbs",
  cohorts   = c("luad", "lusc"),
  threads   = 8,
  scheduler = "slurm",
  slurm     = list(partition = "cpu", mem = "48G", time = "2-00:00:00",
                   cpus_per_task = 8, account = "mylab")
)
pgvis_init(cfg)
```

## Sample sheet

Three columns: cohort, tissue, sample. Validate it *before* queuing a thousand
jobs behind it — the check catches the failure modes that otherwise surface
six hours in.

```{r sheet}
sheet <- data.frame(
  cohort = c("luad", "luad", "lusc"),
  tissue = c("blood", "solid", "blood"),
  sample = c("PT-001", "PT-001", "PT-002")
)
pgvis_sample_sheet(sheet,
                   path    = file.path(cfg$root, "samples.tsv"),
                   bam_dir = "/data/raw_bams")
#> Warning: 1/3 samples have no BAM under /data/raw_bams. First few: PT-002
```

The GVCF output path is built from cohort/tissue/sample, so duplicate rows
would silently overwrite each other — that is an error, not a warning.

## Running the stages

```{r run}
pgvis_merge_bams(cfg, "samples.tsv", submit = TRUE)
pgvis_call_gvcf(cfg,  "samples.tsv", submit = TRUE)   # array over chromosomes
pgvis_combine_gvcf(cfg,    submit = TRUE)              # array over cohort x chr
pgvis_genotype_filter(cfg, submit = TRUE)
pgvis_vcf_to_bed(cfg,      submit = TRUE)
pgvis_intersect(cfg,       submit = TRUE)              # array over features
```

Leave `submit = FALSE` (the default) to render without running:

```{r inspect}
script <- pgvis_call_gvcf(cfg, "samples.tsv")
cat(readLines(script)[1:25], sep = "\n")
```

### Restartability

Every stage skips outputs that already exist and are non-empty. A job killed
by walltime is simply resubmitted; there is no separate "rerun the failed
ones" path to maintain. Outputs are written to a temporary file and moved into
place only on success, so an interrupted job never leaves a truncated file
that the next run would mistake for finished work.

To force a redo:

```{r force}
pgvis_intersect(cfg, submit = TRUE, PGVIS_FORCE = 1)
```

Any extra named argument becomes a shell variable, which is also how you
override a default without editing the template:

```{r override}
pgvis_genotype_filter(
  cfg, submit = TRUE,
  FILTER_EXPR = "QD < 2.0 || FS > 60.0 || MQ < 40.0",
  JAVA_MEM    = "32g"
)
```

## What comes out

Stage 5 writes a headerless BED, one row per ALT allele, with allele counts
and the list of carrying samples:

```
chr1  1000  1001  A  G   1  snv  2  0.333  6  2  S1,S3
chr1  2000  2002  CT C   1  del  1  0.167  6  1  S1
chr1  2000  2002  CT CTT 2  ins  2  0.333  6  2  S2,S3
```

The carrier list and the genotype columns come from a single `awk` pass over
the VCF, so sample order cannot drift out of sync with the genotypes. The
column layout is the `"cohort"` block of `pgvis_schema()`; if you change the
awk emitter, change the schema to match.

Stage 6 intersects against the regulatory regions and then dbSNP, producing
`06_dbsnp/<feature>/<cohort>_chr<N>_dbsnp.bed`.

## Reading it back into R

```{r load}
variants <- pgvis_load_variants(cfg)
pgvis_qc(variants)
pgvis_summarise_by(variants, by = c("cohort", "feature_type"))
```

`pgvis_load_variants()` applies the schema, splits multi-allelic dbSNP
records, resolves the population frequency and builds the coordinate keys, so
what comes back is one tidy table ready to analyse.

Run `pgvis_qc()` before going further. The two findings worth stopping for are
a majority of variants with no matched population frequency (usually a dbSNP
build mismatch, or the frequency-source indices being wrong for your track
version — see `pgvis_freq_sources()`) and variants with zero carriers, which
means the genotype columns were misparsed.

## Reference panel arm

The 1000 Genomes side is the same pipeline with three differences, all
handled by arguments: the VCFs are already jointly genotyped so stages 1–4 are
skipped, the intersection column order is reversed, and ancestry comes from
the panel pedigree.

```{r panel}
panel <- pgvis_panel_config(
  root    = "/scratch/me/1kgp_pgvis",
  vcf_dir = "/refs/1kgp/vcf",
  regions = cfg$regions,
  dbsnp_dir = cfg$dbsnp_dir
)
pgvis_init(panel)

pgvis_vcf_to_bed(panel, submit = TRUE)
pgvis_intersect(panel,  submit = TRUE)

panel_variants <- pgvis_load_variants(panel, region_first = FALSE)
ped <- pgvis_load_pedigree("/refs/1kgp/20130606_g1k_3202_samples_ped_population.txt")
```

Then score each arm against its own variant list, stack the two arms and
standardise against the reference:

```{r bind}
cohort_per_sample <- pgvis_sample_scores(pgvis_variant_score(cohort_long))
panel_per_sample  <- pgvis_sample_scores(pgvis_variant_score(panel_long))
stacked <- pgvis_bind_panel(cohort_per_sample, panel_per_sample)
scores  <- pgvis_score(stacked, reference_group = "1000Genomes")
```

`pgvis_bind_panel()` refuses to proceed if the two arms share no
superpopulation, which would otherwise produce a table of `NA` z-scores rather
than an error.

## Provenance

`pgvis_run()` writes a manifest next to every result recording the thresholds,
the scoring method and reference statistics, the input row counts and any QC warnings.

```{r manifest}
pgvis_manifest(cfg, stage = "custom_filter",
               inputs  = list(n_in = nrow(variants)),
               outputs = list(rds = "filtered.rds"))
```

Months later, when you need to know exactly which thresholds produced a given
table, the answer sits next to the result rather than depending on memory.
